items.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong- Jeremy Schon & Greg Ormont interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 8, 2024

ctx.x: You’ve cracked the code. I mean we’ve, as a band you know and as individual people, we’ve always, I mean we all listen to a lot of instrumental music, especially like kind of groove-oriented instrumental music you know like people like John Scofield more in the jazz world. And like we love to be able to vamp on a cool groove. If there’s anything that, you know, for “Horizon” I feel like we thought all right, the simple guitar melody that’s happening is very simple, but it catchy enough. And I don’t know, somehow…

And in those instances you know, like Jeremy wrote the bulk of that song and when he does he’ll send them my way usually or I’ll be sitting next to him in college or whatever the time period is. And I’ll think about adding vocals, almost always, where we sing often. We have a lot of instrumentals but the majority have vocals. And the intro I ended up, you know coming across this like idea, and the song kind of harkened me back to some other concerts I’ve been to where there’s a vamp that’s building and you kind…

soak in the bliss of it. You soak in the patience of it and just kind of be there in the moment, and you know it’s kind of the preparation before the build. You know? And intro vocals talk about this, like I walk into the show, I finally hang my coat, you know, find my seating and enjoy the show. And then the song basically starts and I thought it was so like peaceful and warm and happy that it can live on its own and after the entire journey of the song where it goes from happy and peaceful to like has the…
